---
title: "Turbo Remote Cache"
description: "Self-hosted Turborepo remote cache on Cloudflare R2: trust model, configuration, cost bounds, cutover, and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-10-23"
---

`apps/turbo-cache` is a Cloudflare Worker that implements the Turborepo remote
cache API (`/v8/artifacts`) on an R2 bucket. It replaces the Vercel-hosted
remote cache, which stays the fallback until cutover. It ships **disabled**:
`TURBO_CACHE_MODE` defaults to `off`, which serves nothing and performs no
billable storage operations. For cache layers and miss debugging, see
the Caching page (`apps/docs/build/devops/caching.mdx`).

## Design

- **Keys:** artifacts are stored at `v1/<scope>/<hash>`. The scope comes from
  the server-side token registry, never from the client's `teamId` or `slug`,
  so a client cannot choose where its artifacts land.
- **Tokens:** `TURBO_CACHE_TOKENS` is a JSON list of
  `{ "id", "sha256", "read": [scopes], "write"?: scope }`. The registry stores
  only SHA-256 digests of tokens and compares them in constant time. A writer
  may write only the first scope it reads. One malformed entry disables the
  whole registry (fail closed).
- **Signatures:** with `TURBO_CACHE_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=true` (the default),
  uploads without an `x-artifact-tag` are rejected. Clients sign and verify
  with `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY` when `turbo.json` sets
  `remoteCache.signature: true`, so a stored artifact that was not signed with
  the shared key is rejected by every reader.
- **Bounds:** artifacts are capped at 100 MiB (ceiling 500 MiB). Artifacts
  older than the TTL (default 7 days, ceiling 30) are served as misses even if
  the R2 lifecycle rule lags. Batch queries accept at most 50 hashes. A rate
  limiter allows 600 requests per token per 10 seconds.
- **Durable stop fence:** a single `TurboCacheBudget` Durable Object admits
  every billable operation:
  - Daily class A (writes), daily class B (reads) and daily write-byte caps
    pause that class until the next UTC day.
  - Crossing the monthly class A fence trips a durable stop that only an
    operator reset clears.
  - An unavailable budget object counts as a pause, never as an allowance.
  - Denied reads return a miss, so Turbo runs the task; that costs time and
    never yields a stale result. Denied writes return `503`.
- **Admin:** `GET /admin/budget` and `POST /admin/fence`
  (`{"action":"trip"}` or `{"action":"reset"}`) require the admin token, whose
  SHA-256 is `TURBO_CACHE_ADMIN_TOKEN_SHA256`.

## Trust model

| Client | Token | Reads | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trusted `main` and `production` CI jobs | `gha-main` | `main` | `main` |
| Same-repository branch CI (optional, needs CI security owner sign-off) | `gha-branches` | `branches`, `main` | `branches` |
| Fork pull requests and Dependabot | none (GitHub withholds secrets) | — | — |
| Trusted local machines and devboxes | one token per machine | `local-<id>`, `main` | `local-<id>` |
| Untrusted agent sandboxes | read-only token | `main` | — |

`main` artifacts are written only by trusted `main` CI, so branch, machine and
sandbox clients can reuse them but never poison them. Clients can additionally
enforce read-only at the client with `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_READ_ONLY=1` (or
`TURBO_CACHE=local:rw,remote:r`).

## Configuration names

Set these values by name only. Never commit them.

Worker secrets (owner creates them with the cf CLI or the dashboard):

- `TURBO_CACHE_TOKENS`: JSON token registry, digests only.
- `TURBO_CACHE_ADMIN_TOKEN_SHA256`: digest of the admin token.

Worker variables (in `apps/turbo-cache/cloudflare.config.ts`):

- `TURBO_CACHE_MODE`: `off` (default), `read-only`, or `read-write`.
- `TURBO_CACHE_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE`, `TURBO_CACHE_TTL_DAYS`,
  `TURBO_CACHE_MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES`, `TURBO_CACHE_DAILY_CLASS_A`,
  `TURBO_CACHE_DAILY_CLASS_B`, `TURBO_CACHE_DAILY_WRITE_BYTES`,
  `TURBO_CACHE_MONTHLY_CLASS_A_FENCE`. Missing or malformed values fall back
  to defaults, and overrides are clamped to hard ceilings.

Cloudflare resources (owner creates):

- R2 bucket `tuturuuu-turbo-cache` with a lifecycle rule that deletes objects
  under `v1/` after 7 days.
- Custom domain `turbo-cache.tuturuuu.com` on the Worker.

GitHub repository settings (owner sets at cutover):

- Variable `TURBO_API`: `https://turbo-cache.tuturuuu.com`.
- Variable `TURBO_TEAM`: any stable slug. The Worker ignores it for scoping.
- Secret `TURBO_TOKEN`: the `gha-main` token, replacing the Vercel token.
- Secret `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY`: at least 32 random bytes, shared
  by every trusted client.

Local trusted machines (shell profile or secret store, never `.env`):
`TURBO_API`, `TURBO_TEAM`, `TURBO_TOKEN`, and
`TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY`.

## Cost estimate

From the 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-23 CI inventory:

- Test, Type Check, Coverage, Mail Calendar Tasks, Meet and Parley run about
  303,000 Turbo task lookups per week. Vercel and release builds add about
  20,000.
- Runs on `main` produce about 40,000 of those lookups. Those are the only
  writes under the default trust model.

Each lookup costs one Worker request, one Durable Object request and one R2
class B operation, or two class B operations when a branch token checks both
of its scopes. Each upload costs the same plus one class A operation.

| Item | Expected per month | Included in plan | Expected cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R2 class B (reads) | about 1.4M to 2.8M | 10M | $0 |
| R2 class A (writes, `main` only) | up to about 175,000 | 1M | $0 |
| R2 class A (with branch writes) | up to about 430,000 | 1M | $0 |
| R2 storage (7-day TTL) | 10 to 30 GB | 10 GB | up to about $0.30 |
| Worker requests | about 1.5M | 10M on Workers Paid | $0 |
| Durable Object requests | about 1.5M | 1M | about $0.08 |

The defaults cap the worst case independently of traffic:

- Class A is fenced at 2M per month, so at most about $4.50 above the
  included 1M.
- Class B is capped at 1M per day, so at most about $7.20 per month above
  the included 10M.
- Daily write bytes are capped at 20 GiB, and the TTL bounds storage near
  140 GiB, about $2 per month.
- Durable Object admission requests stop when a daily cap trips, because the
  isolate memoizes the denial for 60 seconds.

The total default envelope is under $20 per month. Ingress rate limits and
billing alerts are smoothing and notification only; the budget object is the
spend bound.

## Cutover checklist

1. Owner creates the R2 bucket, its 7-day `v1/` lifecycle rule, the custom
   domain, and the two Worker secrets. Generate tokens locally, store only
   their SHA-256 digests in `TURBO_CACHE_TOKENS`, and hand the raw tokens to
   their holders through the secret store.
2. Deploy the Worker with `TURBO_CACHE_MODE=off`. Confirm
   `GET /v8/artifacts/status` returns `disabled` and that the R2 operation
   metrics stay at zero.
3. Set `TURBO_CACHE_MODE=read-write`. From one trusted machine, run a small
   task twice with the new `TURBO_API` and token, then confirm a `remote` hit
   and the budget counters (`GET /admin/budget`).
4. Pass `api: ${{ vars.TURBO_API }}` and
   `signature-key: ${{ secrets.TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY }}` to
   `.github/actions/run-with-turbo-remote-cache` under the existing trusted
   conditions. Set the repository variable and secrets. Replace
   `TURBO_TOKEN` with the `gha-main` token.
5. Enable `remoteCache.signature: true` and
   `futureFlags.longerSignatureKey: true` in `turbo.json`. Existing unsigned
   artifacts then miss once and are rewritten signed.
6. Watch one week of budget counters against this estimate before adding
   branch or machine writers.

## Rollback

- **Fast stop:** `POST /admin/fence` with `{"action":"trip"}`, or set
  `TURBO_CACHE_MODE=off`. Clients then see misses and run tasks; no build
  fails because of the cache.
- **Return to Vercel:** delete the `TURBO_API` variable, which makes the
  wrapper unset `TURBO_API`, and restore the Vercel token to `TURBO_TOKEN`.
  Keep the Vercel token in the owner's secret store until the self-hosted
  cache has run a full week within budget.
- Signed artifacts are not required for the Vercel fallback. Revert step 5 if
  Vercel clients lack the signature key.
